name: Maiden's Tears Waterfall
full: Maiden's Tears Waterfall (Maiden's Braids, Kok-Jaiyk Waterfall) — Jeti-Oguz
near: The Jeti-Oguz resort (sanatorium) — 3.6 km to the north (silkadv.com); the Kok-Jaiyk tract/jailoo (summer pasture) with yurt camps — 1.5 km to the southeast, the start of the trail. Jeti-Oguz village — 12 km below the resort; Karakol — ~28–35 km.
elev: 2400–2500 m: 2GIS — 2400 m; silkadv — 2470 m; catalog — ~2500 m. This is the elevation of the waterfall, not the height of the drop.
short: A waterfall in a spruce side valley above the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo in the Jeti-Oguz gorge: water 20–50 m high (depending on the source) runs down a sloping rock wall in many streams, “like tears”; 30–50 minutes on foot or by horse from the yurt camps, free entry.
desc: The waterfall is known by two names — “Maiden's Tears” and “Maiden's Braids” (the Kyrgyz landmark being Kok-Jaiyk): 2GIS, Kaktus.media and the catalog use “Tears”, while silkadv, Google and English-language guides use “Braids/Maiden's Braids”; the coordinates in all sources converge on one point 1.5 km northwest of the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo and 3.6 km south of the Jeti-Oguz resort, so it is one and the same place. The water runs down a sloping rock 5–10 m wide among Tian Shan spruces and fallen trunks; the height of the drop is given in sources as from 20 m (Kaktus.media, 2016) to 40 m (silkadv, catalog) and 50 m (2GIS). The trail from Kok-Jaiyk is 2.5 km round trip with an ascent of ~160 m (Asia Hikes, 07.2024), narrow, on dark soil, muddy and slippery after rain; horses are offered at the camps (800 som for the first kilometer of the climb, 2024). A local belief: a girl who washes in the waterfall will soon marry (2GIS). There is no entrance fee (2024). The classic day from Karakol: the “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” rocks, the resort, the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo, the waterfall.
guide: Don't look on the maps for “Maiden's Tears” and “Maiden's Braids” as two different places — it is one waterfall above Kok-Jaiyk, and drivers know it by either name. From the yurts the trail takes half an hour to an hour: narrow, in the spruce forest, and turning to mud after rain, so bring shoes with good tread, and a horse (about 800 som) makes sense only for the first kilometer. Come in June–July, when there is the most water — in August the streams are thinner. Washing in the waterfall, according to the local belief, means a quick wedding. Leave an hour for the jailoo itself: yurts, kumys and a view of the “Seven Bulls” from the upper trail.
see: The waterfall itself on a sloping rock among the spruces; the trail through the spruce forest with views of Kok-Jaiyk; the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo with yurt camps; lower down the gorge — the “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” rocks, and the Jeti-Oguz resort with radon baths; higher up the valley — trails to Teleti and Lake Ala-Kul.
skip: You are going in late August–September — there is little water and the waterfall is “thin”. It is raining: the trail is dangerously slippery. You are short on time in Jeti-Oguz — the “Seven Bulls” rocks are more impressive.
diff: Easy–moderate: 2.5 km round trip, +161 m, 30–50 min one way (Asia Hikes 2024; 2GIS 40–50 min); a narrow trail, mud after rain; manageable for children from 6–7 years old.
when: June — early July — maximum water (snowmelt); July–August — the season of yurts and horses at Kok-Jaiyk; September — less water, but dry and empty. In winter access to Kok-Jaiyk over snow is not guaranteed.
hours: Open terrain, 24 hours, no ticket offices (Asia Hikes 2024: no fee). The yurt camps at Kok-Jaiyk — June–September.
daytime: Morning: the waterfall is in the shade of the spruces, the trail is drier and there are no tourists; in the afternoon in July–August — thunderstorms and crowds from the resort.
how: From Karakol: marshrutka (minibus) No. 355 to the Jeti-Oguz resort (100 som) or No. 371 to the village (80 som) + a shared taxi village — resort 50 som (Adventures of Nicole, 10.2026; Asia Hikes 2024); from the resort 3–4 km on foot up the jeep road to Kok-Jaiyk, or a taxi; from the yurts, a 1.2 km trail to the northwest to the waterfall. Taxi Karakol — Jeti-Oguz 1000–1200 som one way, shared ~250 som/person (2026).
needcar: To the resort — there is a marshrutka; to Kok-Jaiyk — on foot 1–1.5 h or by car (SUV/taxi); beyond that only on foot or on horseback.
self: Yes: the trail is obvious from the yurts (ask for the “waterfall”), no permits or payment; an offline map (maps.me/OsmAnd) shows the trail.
roadtype: Paved Karakol — village — resort; from the resort to Kok-Jaiyk, a dirt jeep road (3–4 km, mud after rain); to the waterfall, a narrow footpath/horse trail on dark soil (silkadv, Asia Hikes).
traveltime: Karakol — resort 40–60 min (marshrutka); resort — Kok-Jaiyk 1–1.5 h on foot / 15–20 min by car; Kok-Jaiyk — waterfall 30–50 min one way (2.5 km loop, Asia Hikes 2024; 2GIS 40–50 min).
stay: Yurt camps at Kok-Jaiyk: EcoTrek, Taberik, Golden Yurt (Asia Hikes, 2024) — a guide of ~700 som/person/night (Adventures of Nicole, 2026); the Jeti-Oguz sanatorium at the resort; guesthouses in Jeti-Oguz village and Karakol. Booking — CBT Karakol, Destination Jeti Oguz.
net: At the resort and in the village there is operator coverage; at Kok-Jaiyk and the waterfall coverage is unstable/absent (from reports on Jeti-Oguz; no direct tests found). An offline map is a must.
entry: Free: there is no fee for Kok-Jaiyk and the waterfall (Asia Hikes, 12.07.2024); kyrgyzstanplanner 2026 mentions no fees. The sanatorium and its grounds are separate.
transfer: Marshrutka 80–120 som (2026); taxi Karakol — Jeti-Oguz 1000–1200 som (2026); shared ride village — resort 50 som (2024); a horse to the waterfall 800 som (2024); a tour from Karakol from $85 (2026).
bring: Trekking shoes with good tread, a rain jacket, water, cash (horses, yurts, marshrutka), repellent (June–July), a warm layer for the jailoo (2400 m, cold in the evening).
warn: The trail is narrow and slippery after rain, in places “two people can't pass each other” (Trip to Kyrgyzstan); horses churn up the trail. Do not confuse it with the waterfalls of the same name, “Maiden's Braids” on Elbrus and “Maiden's Tears” in Abkhazia — in searches they overshadow the Kyrgyz one. A marshrutka “to the village” will leave you 12 km from the resort — check the final stop. The last marshrutkas back are ~16–17 h.
food: In the Kok-Jaiyk yurts: kumys, boorsoks, lagman, shashlik, home-baked bread (seasonal, prices negotiable); at the resort — the sanatorium canteen; in Karakol — ashlyan-fu. Specific eateries have not been checked.
reviews: 2GIS “Maiden's Tears Waterfall”: 4.7/5, 26 ratings, 10 reviews (07.10.2026). Google “Maiden's Braids Waterfall” — there is a pin, the rating was not captured. Pluses from 2024–2026 reports: a short scenic climb, spruce forest, free; minuses — mud after rain, horse handlers at the camps, little water at the end of summer.
p.sum: From Karakol — marshrutka No. 355 to the Jeti-Oguz resort (≈100 som) or a taxi (1,000–1,200 som), then 3–4 km along the jeep road on foot (1–1.5 h) or by SUV to the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo, and from the yurts 30–50 minutes along a narrow trail through the spruce forest (2.5 km loop, +160 m). Entry is free, a horse to the waterfall ~800 som. It is best in June — early July when the water is high, and in the morning; you can stay overnight in the Kok-Jaiyk yurt camps (EcoTrek, Taberik, Golden Yurt; a guide of ~700 som/person per place) or in Karakol.

p.season: June — early July — maximum water; July–August — yurts and horses, thunderstorms and crowds from the resort after lunch; September — little water, dry, empty; October–May — yurts closed, Kok-Jaiyk under snow. Ticks and mosquitoes — June–July.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka 100×2; entry free; a yurt ~700 (without food) + food 600–800; a horse optional 800. ≈ 1,500–2,500 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: Taxi 1,000–1,200 one way or a €240 tour per group (÷4 ≈ 5,300 som); lunch in a yurt; horse 800. ≈ 6,000–8,000 som/person.
p.permits: Not needed; there is no fee for Kok-Jaiyk and the waterfall (Asia Hikes 2024). The sanatorium and its services are separate.
p.access: Children from 6–7 years old — on foot; older people — by car to Kok-Jaiyk, to the waterfall on horseback (800 som) or skip it; wheelchair — no (dirt, a narrow trail); dog — allowed, but be careful with horses and shepherd dogs.
